 4            PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that, pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §§ 1332, 1441, and 1446,

 5 Defendant Cloudflare, Inc. (“Cloudflare”) hereby removes to this Court the state court action titled
 6 Eugeniu Turuta and Radu Turuta v. Cloudflare, Inc., et al., San Francisco Superior Court Case
 7 No. CGC-24-615196, filed by Plaintiffs Eugeniu Turuta and Radu Turuta (“Plaintiffs”). This
 8 Court has diversity jurisdiction over this action because the parties are completely diverse and the
 9 amount in controversy exceeds $75,000, exclusive of interest and costs.
10                                    BACKGROUND AND PLEADINGS

11            1.       On June 4, 2024, Plaintiffs filed this lawsuit and their Complaint against

12 Cloudflare, Inc., (“Defendant”), and Does 1 through 30 in the California Superior Court for the
13 County of San Francisco. A copy of the Complaint, including Exhibits A and B thereto, is
14 attached hereto as Exhibit 1.
15                                       TIMELINESS OF REMOVAL

16            2.       The first date upon which Defendant received a copy of the Complaint was June

17 13, 2024, when the Defendant was served by personal service with a copy of the Complaint and a
18 summons from the above referenced state court. A copy of proof of service of summons on
19 Defendant is attached hereto as Exhibit 2.
20            3.       Pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1446(b), Defendant files this Notice of Removal within 30

21 days of service of the Summons and Complaint. See Murphy Brothers, Inc. v. Michetti Pipe
22 Stringing, 526 U.S. 344, 354 (1999). Defendant has therefore timely removed this action.
23 Destfino v. Reiswig, 630 F.3d 952, 956 (9th Cir. 2011) (“each defendant is entitled to thirty days to
24 exercise his removal rights after being served”).
25                                               JURISDICTION

26            4.       This is a civil action of which this Court has original jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C.

27 § 1332 and is one which may be removed to this Court by Defendant pursuant to 28 U.S.C.
28 § 1441(a) in that this is a civil action between citizens of a foreign country and a corporation

 1 domiciled in a State, and the amount in controversy exceeds the sum of $75,000 exclusive of

 3 (“the forum defendant rule embodied in § 1441(b) is a procedural requirement, and thus a
 4 violation of this rule constitutes a waivable non-jurisdictional defect subject to the 30-day time
 5 limit imposed by § 1447(c).”). Plaintiffs seek recognition of a foreign-country money judgment
 6 for the sum of €1,276,864.00 in damages, 25,100 MDL for trial court costs, and 18,825 MDL for
 7 costs of the appeal. (Complaint at p. 3.)
 8            5.       Complete diversity of citizenship exists in that, on information and belief,

 9 Plaintiffs are citizens of Moldova, and Defendant corporation is domiciled in Delaware.
10 (Complaint at p. 1.) There are no unserved defendants, and all named defendants join in this
11 Notice of Removal. Defendant is not required to investigate the identity of unnamed Doe
12 defendants or to obtain their consent for removal. See Newcombe v. Adolf Coors Co., 157 F.3d
13 686, 690-91 (9th Cir. 1998); 28 U.S.C. § 1441(a).
14                       NOTICE TO PLAINTIFFS AND THE SUPERIOR COURT

15            6.       In compliance with 28 U.S.C. § 1446(d), Defendant will serve written notice of the

16 filing of this Notice of Removal on all parties and will also file and serve appropriate notice with
17 the Superior Court of California in and for San Francisco.
18                                               CONCLUSION

19            7.       For the foregoing reasons, this Court has jurisdiction and Defendant requests this

20 Court proceed with this matter as if Plaintiffs had originally filed their complaint in the United
21 States District Court for the Northern District of California.
